title: Discrete PT-symmetric solitons on branched lattices: Vertex states, stability, and vortices
authors: M. Akramov, A. Fayzullaev, O. Tojakhmadova, T. Akhmadjanov
abstract: Branching fundamentally modifies nonlinear localization by introducing vertex degrees of freedom absent in one-dimensional lattices. We investigate localized states in a PT-symmetric four-edge star graph described by the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation. We identify a discrete vortex state with a fixed topological charge, supported by the branching geometry. Constructed by continuation from the anticontinuum limit, the vortex evolves into a current-carrying state in the presence of balanced gain and loss and exhibits stability windows absent for the conventional branches. A possible electric-circuit realization of the proposed model is discussed.
summary: This paper analyzes discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equations on a branched star graph under $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry, revealing that the branching geometry supports a unique, stable vortex soliton. This vortex state possesses a fixed topological charge and exhibits stability regions inaccessible to standard linear or nonlinear soliton solutions on simple chains. The findings suggest new avenues for designing stable waveguiding structures in complex quantum networks.
main_problem: The study investigates localized states (solitons) in Parity-Time ($\mathcal{PT}$)-symmetric systems when the underlying lattice structure is branched, moving beyond simple one-dimensional chains.
main_result: The authors identify a novel, stable vortex state characterized by a fixed topological charge and a non-zero vertex current, which exists in stability windows unavailable in conventional linear or nonlinear branches.
method: The research employs analytical continuation from the anticontinuum limit, combined with linear stability analysis using perturbation theory to determine the stability of the found solutions.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLDS) applied to a branched lattice, specifically a four-edge star graph, incorporating localized Gaussian gain and loss terms to enforce $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry.
key_observables: Topological charge (winding number $\ell$), vertex current ($	ext{J}$), and the complex growth rate ($\lambda$) from the stability analysis.
important_parameters: Gain/loss coefficients ($\gamma_0$), coupling coefficients ($\kappa_0, \kappa_1$), and the spectral eigenvalue ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry reduction for continuation and relies on the invertibility of the Jacobian matrix for continuation methods.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the shift of the $\mathcal{PT}$ phase transition threshold, the numerical continuation of soliton branches (power/amplitude profiles), and the stability regions in parameter space ($\kappa_1$ vs. $\gamma_0$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general NLDS framework on the branched lattice, then using continuation methods to find soliton solutions, and finally characterizing the unique vortex branch via topological invariants and stability analysis.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems as it explores how complex network topologies (branching) fundamentally alter the existence and stability of nonlinear localized excitations (solitons) under non-Hermitian (PT-symmetric) conditions.

Figure 2: Numerical continuation of discrete PT -symmetric solitons bifurcating from the anticontinuum limit for the parameters κ0 = 1, κ1 = 0.4, γ0 = 0.1, σ = 2.5, g = 1. a) total power P = P n(|un|2 + |vn|2) versus µ for the two soliton branches, blue for the stable and red for the unstable solitons; black dots mark the representative points examined in the middle and right columns. b) and c) soliton amplitude profiles |ωn|2, with red and blue dots denoting the gain and loss sites, respectively, and d) and e) the corresponding linear stability spectrum Im[λ] versus Re[λ].

Figure 3: The star graph with four discrete edges. The central quadrimer denotes the vertex block Ω0; red and blue dots mark the gain and loss sites, respectively, on each of the four semi-infinite edges.

Figure 4: Maximal imaginary part of the eigenvalue µ of the linear vertex operator H in Eq. (25) versus γ0, for three values of the localization σ. Other parameters are chosen as follows: κ0 = 1, κ1 = 1.2. For each σ, max[Im(µ)] vanishes below a critical γ0, marking the onset of PT -symmetry breaking. This threshold increases as the gain-loss profile becomes more localized (smaller σ), consistent with the chain result of Fig. 1.

Blue segments denote stable and red segments unstable solutions. Black dots mark the representative points examined in panels (b)–(e). (b),(c) Soliton amplitude profiles at κ1 = 1.5 for the (+) branch and κ1 = 3.5 for the (−) branch, respectively, with red dots corresponding to |u±j,n| and blue dots to |v±j,n|.
